solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get back on with putsch

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter's subject line
a putsch is a coup, a sudden seizure of power

explanation.surface: Someone recovers their position by staging a coup.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup losses is to recover them, so it is a synonym of getting something back.

clue.text: Regular and predictable movement late in the day

parts.note: even means regular, steady
the tide moves in and out on a predictable schedule

explanation.surface: Steady, foreseeable motion as evening approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase: the late part of the day, evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the late part of the day.

clue.text: Such an office aiming to eliminate handwriting?

definitions.text: Such an office aiming to eliminate handwriting?

parts.words: Such an office aiming to eliminate handwriting?
parts.note: a plan for zero pens, abolishing handwriting, as well as a type of office layout

explanation.surface: A modern office keen to go paperless and pen-free.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as O (nothing) + PEN + PLAN: a plan for no pens.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan office has no partition walls, a common modern workspace layout.

clue.text: Yearn extremely to visit the ends of the earth: one reaches a group of islands

indicators.note: visiting puts the yearn letters inside the poles

parts.note: the poles are the ends of the earth's axis

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of yearn

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An explorer longs to travel to the far ends of the earth and reaches some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ends of the earth' looks like a figure of speech for remote places; here it is the North and South Poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is the huge collection of Pacific island groups including Hawaii, Samoa and Tonga.

clue.text: Getting at bandleader wearing nothing ostentatious

indicators.note: the bandleader's letter is clothed by the other words, so it sits inside them

parts.note: NO means none, nothing
BLING is showy, ostentatious jewellery; used here as an adjective
the leader, or first letter, of band is B

explanation.surface: A modestly dressed conductor is bribing or nobbling someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting at' is British slang for bribing or tampering with someone, the same sense as nobbling a jury or a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble a juror or horse is to tamper with or bribe it, which British idiom also calls getting at.

clue.text: One of Jane's, her baby not unusually filled with rage

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are filled with rage, which goes inside them
unusually signals the letters of her baby not are put in an unusual order

parts.note: anger is rage

explanation.surface: A baby filled with fury, not behaving as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' makes NORTHABBEY from her baby not, and 'filled with' puts ANGER inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Northanger Abbey is a novel by Jane Austen, so it is one of Jane's books.

clue.text: Confirm escape of wild animal?

definitions.meaning: to ... a claim is to confirm it
taken literally, a ... of its enclosure has escaped

explanation.surface: Verifying reports that a beast is on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that bears out a story supports it; read literally, a loose bear has got out.

clue.text: Start bland description of restaurant experience

definitions.meaning: to begin something, as a verb
a punning sense: the answer split into four short words gives a flat account of eating out

explanation.surface: A dull summary of dining out somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Split INITIATE as IN IT I ATE: a deadpan report of a restaurant meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to begin it, a synonym of start as a verb.

clue.text: Suspended, getting in bloody fast

indicators.note: the suspended word gets into the bloody one, inside it

parts.note: gory means bloody
hung means suspended

explanation.surface: A hanging in a bloody manner, reported grimly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' is a verb meaning to not eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to abstain from food, which is going hungry.

clue.text: Old radical populist with two pounds in bank at end of year

indicators.note: the two pounds are placed in the bank, so they go inside it

parts.note: a levee is a riverside embankment
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two pounds give LL

indicators.note: the end of the word year is its final letter

explanation.surface: A populist banks two pounds just before the year ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The Levellers were a radical political movement during the English Civil War of the 1640s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levellers were seventeenth-century English radicals demanding equal rights, so one member was an old radical populist.

clue.text: In bowl, article that may accompany coffee,

indicators.note: the article is put in the bowl, so it goes inside

parts.note: a dish is a bowl
AN is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something served in a bowl alongside a cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'something that may accompany coffee': a Danish pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish is a sweet pastry, commonly eaten with a morning coffee.

clue.text: A sort of dance? Move slowly if necessary

parts.note: tap is a style of dance
to inch is to move slowly, little by little

explanation.surface: A dancer edging forward cautiously, questioning what kind of dance it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'at a pinch' means in an emergency, when there is no better option.

clue.text: Thought anyone but myself available

parts.note: anyone but me is 'not I', giving NOT I
ON means available, as in a dish being on the menu

explanation.surface: Someone thinks anybody except themselves is free.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or belief, a synonym of a thought as a noun.

clue.text: Similar-sounding old name given to animal and insect

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An outdated label is attached to a beast and a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonant describes words whose vowel sounds echo each other, so they resemble one another in sound.

clue.text: Wicked Olympic city unfortunately unsafe to tour

indicators.note: touring around the city means the jumbled letters go round it
unfortunately signals that the letters of unsafe come out badly arranged

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics

explanation.surface: An Olympic host city is too dangerous to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns unsafe into NEFAUS, which 'to tour' wraps around RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means villainous or criminal, a synonym of wicked.

clue.text: Stage a new abridged production of The Cherry Orchard

indicators.note: only a cut-down portion of the words is produced, so the answer is concealed within them

explanation.surface: A theatre company mounts a shortened revival of Chekhov's play The Cherry Orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'staGE A New'; the play's title supplies the definition, cherry, with 'The' and 'Orchard' as surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The gean is the wild cherry tree of Europe, so it is a kind of cherry.

clue.text: Really great performance — furious father's left

parts.note: a gig is a musical performance

indicators.note: father has left, so his letters depart from the word for furious

parts.note: frantic means furious, wild
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A wild concert after which an angry dad walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s left' takes FR out of FRANTIC, leaving ANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means huge, which is very great in size.

clue.text: Lily has a special house key

parts.note: Del is the delete key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A flower owns a special key to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a flowering plant of the lily family.

clue.text: Fresh United back finally ready

indicators.note: back tells us the word for united is read in reverse

parts.note: to wed is to unite, so united gives WED

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of ready

explanation.surface: A football team's revived defender is at last fit to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United back' looks like a football player; it is WED turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy means fresh and young, as in dewy-eyed or dew-fresh.

clue.text: Some medicine stolen? One may win in court

parts.note: drops are a liquid medicine
hot is slang for stolen

explanation.surface: Pilfered drugs end up as evidence in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' is the tennis court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop shot is a softly hit tennis stroke landing just over the net, which can win a point.

clue.text: Supply wren with suet feeder

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, the letters bend into a new shape

explanation.surface: Putting suet out for a wren at the bird feeder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is the adverb of supple, flexibly, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet nurse breastfeeds another woman's baby, so she is a feeder.

clue.text: Liked a river, but forced to divert round it

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the a and river, enclosing them
diverting the word forced sends its letters on a new course, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone fond of a river is nonetheless made to reroute around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to divert' makes CEDFOR from forced, and 'round' puts it about A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: If you cared for something you were fond of it, a phrase meaning liked.

clue.text: Is youngster allowed to eat here?

definitions.text: Is youngster allowed to eat here?

parts.note: can means is allowed, as in 'you can go'
a teen is a youngster

explanation.surface: A question about whether a teenager may dine in some place.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'can teen?' the question asks if a young person may eat; the whole clue also describes a canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria in a school or workplace where people eat.

clue.text: Close contract finally, with some help around

indicators.note: the help goes around the last letter of contract, enclosing it

parts.note: some help is a hand, as in 'give me a hand'

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of contract

explanation.surface: Wrapping up a contract with a little assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb to go with contract; it is the adjective meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at hand is nearby and within reach, so it is close.

clue.text: Poison developed from a protein

indicators.note: the letters of a protein are developed into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A toxin produced from a protein in a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade, so it is a poison.

clue.text: Better organised revolutionary holding one childish opponent back

indicators.note: back says the whole string is read in reverse
holding means the revolutionary contains the one

parts.note: RED is a communist revolutionary
I is the Roman numeral one
IT is the chaser in the children's game of tag

explanation.surface: A radical restrains a playground rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses everything before it, the string REIDIT; 'childish opponent' is the chaser in tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidier is the comparative of tidy, meaning neater and better arranged.

clue.text: Members of union run into worries

indicators.note: the run is put into the worries, so it goes inside

parts.note: bothers means worries, as a noun
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Trade union members encounter problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Trade unionists traditionally call each other brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow trade unionists traditionally address one another as brother, so brothers are members of a union.

clue.text: Two dots, for example, representing small island

parts.note: a colon is the punctuation mark made of two dots
say means for example, as in 'a fruit, say an apple'

explanation.surface: A pair of dots on a map stands for a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonsay is a small island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonsay is a small Hebridean island off western Scotland, an example of an island.

clue.text: Me and my best friend?

definitions.meaning: in a crossword, me is the compiler
a dog is man's best friend

explanation.surface: The compiler introduces themselves and their dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter compiles crosswords, and a setter is also a gundog, man's best friend.
